answer: Agents can require each new identity to lock a scarce token in an on-chain bond before it may vote on tasks or claim rewards; the bond is returned only after a delay and can be slashed when independent audits prove duplicate control. This makes a sybil campaign costly: an attacker must tie up capital for every persona and risks losing it, rather than minting identities for free. The onyx pool can fund audits, while zenith marks the bond threshold; raising it too far creates a spiral that excludes honest newcomers.
